title: ArchPilot wire contract
description: Single source of truth for the shapes that cross the Python/TypeScript boundary. Build-scope decision D2 replaced the architects' shared `packages/core` with a Python backend, so nothing in the toolchain reconciles the two languages any more; this file is the replacement (decision D4). It covers (1) the ArchGraph design document shared by designs and patterns - schema 1.0 (flat graph) and schema 2.0 (design-v2 D-08: graph + deployment + brief + decisions + derivations), and (2) three envelope rules, because the review of 2026-09-23 found that envelope drift - not graph drift - caused the first real bug. Validated by ArchPilot/backend/tests/test_contracts.py (jsonschema) and ArchPilot/src/contracts/contract.test.ts (ajv), both driven by fixtures/index.json, and at runtime by backend/app/contract.py. Contract 1.1.0 is additive: every 1.0 document that was valid is still valid. Deliberately NOT an OpenAPI document and deliberately not code-generated.

camelCaseKey.title: Envelope rule (a) - wire casing
camelCaseKey.description: Every key that crosses the HTTP boundary is camelCase, at every depth, including inside an ArchGraph 2.0 document. The SPA's domain types are camelCase throughout (WorkspaceRecord.projectName, EntityEnvelope.schemaVersion, SizingResult.formulaVersion); Python is snake_case. The wire picks camelCase once, here. Backend side: app/schemas.py ApiModel sets alias_generator=to_camel. Consequence for 2.0 (red-team review B2): data never becomes a key. Target ids, node ids and artifact names travel as VALUES inside arrays of objects (deployment.bindings, scenario.placements, derivations), never as map keys.

camelCaseObject.description: Recursively asserts envelope rule (a) over a whole response body. Point any live API response at this to prove no snake_case key slipped in at any depth - including a design response that carries a 2.0 graph.

timestamp.title: Envelope rule (c) - timestamp format
timestamp.description: ISO 8601, always UTC, always with an explicit offset - `2026-09-23T06:26:52+00:00` or `2026-09-23T06:26:52Z`. A naive local timestamp is rejected: JavaScript's Date parses `2026-09-23 06:26:52` as local time and `2026-09-23T06:26:52` as UTC, so an offset-less string means two clients disagree about the same instant. Backend side: datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat().

errorResponse.title: Envelope rule (b) - error shape
errorResponse.description: Every non-2xx JSON body is exactly {detail} or {detail, requestId}. `detail` is a human-readable string, never an object or a list - FastAPI's default RequestValidationError body is a list and is normalised by app/main.py's exception handlers so this rule holds for 4xx as well as 5xx. `requestId` echoes the x-request-id response header so a user can quote one token in a bug report.

archGraph.title: ArchGraph - the one design document, dispatched on schemaVersion
archGraph.description: A user design and a reference pattern serialise to the identical document (architects' decision D1). `schemaVersion` selects the shape: '2.0' is validated as archGraphV2; anything else (including a missing version) is validated as archGraphV1, which is what every document before contract 1.1.0 was. KNOWN LIMIT: JSON Schema cannot express referential integrity, so 'every edge.source names an existing node.id', 'ids are unique', 'no parent cycles' and 'type is a catalogue role' are NOT checked here - they belong to the L1 integrity layer: backend/app/graph_integrity.py and validateGraph() in src/domain/graph/validate.ts, which share the rule codes listed in fixtures/index.json `integrityCases`. This file checks shape; the integrity layer checks consistency.

schemaVersion.description: Pinned (NFR-EXT-002 / NFR2-EXT-004). Adding a version here is the deliberate act that says a migration function exists in src/domain/graph/migrate.ts.

nodeType.description: Schema 1.0 fixed palette (REQ-DESIGN-002). Frozen: schema 2.0 replaced the enum with catalogue roles (contracts/catalog/components.json); the 1.0 -> 2.0 type map is the catalogue's `legacyTypes['1.0']`.

label.description: REQ-DESIGN-003. Required as a key, may be empty: an unlabelled edge is a warning in validateGraph(), not a contract violation.

roleId.description: A logical role id from contracts/catalog/components.json (requirements v2.1 section 4.1.1). The pattern is the contract; catalogue membership is the L1 integrity check (design-v2 D-03), so growing the taxonomy never needs a contract change.

codeName.description: Stable identifier used in generated code and resource addresses (REQ-DES-008). Set once from the label; renaming the label does not change it.

targetId.description: A deployment target kind (aws, vsphere, bare_metal, ...) or a target profile id. Target ids are data, so this is a pattern, not an enum. Only ever used as a VALUE (review B2).

configMap.description: An open map of scalars (or string lists) with camelCase keys. Which keys are meaningful is catalogue or question-catalogue data, checked in TypeScript, so adding a field needs no contract release.

catalogueVersion.description: The components.json version this document was last edited against (review M6/M7: an upstream input of bindings and suggestions).

nodeAttributes.description: Neutral attributes common to every role - requirements v2.1 REQ-DES-024 and REQ-DES-025 names (statefulness, failureDomainLevel, failureDomainLabel), plus design-v2's sizeClass. The enums are mirrored by the catalogue's `attributes` list; a test in each suite asserts they agree. Absent = the role default from the catalogue (containers of type site and zone supply failure-domain defaults to their children).

sizingAttachment.description: Summary of a sizing scenario attached to a node (design-v2 D-11). The full scenario lives in sizing_scenarios; staleness is tracked by `derivations`. `stale: true` is what migration writes for a 1.0 `sizingScenarioId`, whose numbers were never copied into the graph.

archNodeV2.description: A provider-neutral node (NFR2-NEUT-001): logical role, neutral attributes and neutral role config. Everything target-specific lives in deployment.bindings (review B2).

position.description: Relative to the parent container when parentId is set.

config.description: Neutral, role-specific configuration (catalogue field descriptors). Never provider-specific.

edgeMode.description: Mirrored by the catalogue's `edgeModes`; a test in each suite asserts they agree.

kind.description: REQ-DES-005: flow = visual only, no code; access = the source uses the target, so adapters may derive firewall rules, permissions and references (design-v2 D-09).

binding.description: A node's realisation on one target (review B2 / alternative A2). Bindings for every target a node was ever configured on are kept, so re-targeting away and back is lossless (REQ-TGT-005).

realisation.description: A realisation id from that target's catalogue: `<target>.<name>`.

placements.description: Per-node profile overrides (hybrid; REQ-TGT-003 Should). The v1 UI may show a single implicit scenario (review A6); the shape is here so v1.1 needs no data migration.

deployment.title: Deployment-target layer (design-v2 4.3.5 as corrected by review B2)
deployment.description: Absent = no target chosen yet (REQ-TGT-003 default: unset). Templates and patterns carry no deployment (REQ-TPL-004). This is the ONLY subtree of a design document that may contain provider terms; the neutrality scan excludes it and nothing else.

brief.title: Wizard answers and derived artifacts (REQ-WIZ-*, design-v2 4.2.9 / 4.3.8)
brief.description: `context` and `answers` are open maps (review m2): the question catalogue is data, validated in TypeScript, so a new wizard question needs no contract release.

decisionRecord.title: ADR light (REQ-ART-006, design-v2 4.3.9)
decisionRecord.description: Free text is capped at 4000 characters per field and the log at 100 records (review m3), so ADRs cannot crowd out the graph under the 1 MiB cap.

date.description: A calendar date, not a timestamp: the day the decision was taken.

derivation.description: `artifact` was derived from `upstream` when upstream's canonical content hashed to `hash` (REQ-ART-002, design-v2 4.3.10). Stored as an array of values (review B2), so artifact names such as brief.answers never become keys.

archGraphV2.title: ArchGraph 2.0 - the design document (design-v2 D-08)
archGraphV2.description: Logical graph (provider-neutral nodes and edges) plus the deployment-target layer, the wizard brief, the decision log and the outdated-tracking derivations, in one document so the existing designs API, revisions, 409 handling and 1 MiB cap apply unchanged. Limits: nodes 500, edges 1000, decisions 100, derivations 500, profiles 10, scenarios 10.
